raw_text:
The case project is a simulation of a large manufacturing operation.  The case simulates a single production line. A management team is charged with the objective of ensuring an optimal measurement of consumer confidence in order to maximize business objectives. The measurements are used to judge senior management's success as well as strategic business decisions. There are many processes and rules that cover a wide range of decisions and actions. The objective of this sub-project is to use the simulation to determine why some simulated operations relate to similar events show remarkably different completion time.

The simulation engine supports petabyte scale storage of data.  Furthermore, the simulation engine included support for software-testing approaches such as test-driven development and test-first.

The research plan uses a process-aware software-development testing methodology.  The research plan seeks to advance understanding of system dynamics rather than software dynamics.

Data or evidence needed
We need the dataset produced by a simulation system with distributed feed rates and completion times.

The goal is simply to make one set of decisions about working, including the decisions of test first.
We should aim to develop some software tests based on dissatisfaction from the three sites in the case.

The measurements will be completion-time.

The tools and techniques would need to be used to build observation sets (or regressions) which to explain completion times, using analytical facilities.

The stopping rules will define after how many observations we will end the system tests.

The stopping time will be defined for completion-times.

Identify the research design, as explained by sections in the brilliant book Visible Research:

  • Why do sites using the same nominal work process show persistent completion-time differences?
  • What factors account for those differences?
  • How would observations distinguish between competing explanations?
  • What measurements would help prove your explanation?
Write a research plan paper. Simply using the provoking section types as headings to your draft is a fine start. The objective and scope sections should provide a justification for your research, including the results you'll share for the third step.
